summary: ADR-004 declares a cache-first read path with no cache above the storefront — amend the ADR to what exists
description:
### Finding (architecture review R4, 2026-07-25)

ADR-004 declares volatility-tiered TTLs with one cache owner per tier. Verified against the code:

- **The only cache that exists** is `web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts` — an in-process Astro SSR page-data map with single-flight coalescing. It is correct, and it does honor the tier (the middleware derives the outgoing `Cache-Control` from *remaining* freshness, so staleness does not stack).
- **The gateway does not cache.** `gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go` builds a bare `httputil.ReverseProxy` per route. Nothing between it and the services caches anything.
- **Back-office, scanner and service-to-service reads honor no cache at all.** They receive `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` and discard it.

So `Cache-Control` on the service side is presently a declaration with no consumer outside SSR. That is a defensible position — the headers are exactly the contract a future tier needs — but the ADR does not say so, and a reader reasonably concludes a cache tier is deployed.

### Scope discipline

**Docs only.** Building the tier is TKT-31's epic (Read-path caching & hot-event serving). This ticket must not grow a code diff — a source change in the PR is a scope failure, not a bonus.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ADR-004 states which readers honor the volatility tiers today (SSR page-data cache, with single-flight) and which honor nothing (gateway, service-to-service, back-office, scanner).
- [ ] It states that the TTL declarations are a contract for future caches, so the next reader does not mistake them for a deployed tier.
- [ ] The gap is linked to TKT-31, not left implicit.
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md`'s caching line matches.
- [ ] The diff contains **no source changes**.

objective.note: ADR-004 reads as if a cache tier exists. It does not: the only cache honoring the TTL declarations is the Astro SSR page-data cache in one process. Make the ADR describe what is true, and route the actual gap to the epic that owns it.

scope.note: IN: amending ADR-004 to state exactly which readers honor the volatility tiers today and which do not; correcting the caching line in docs/architecture.md; linking the gap to TKT-31. OUT: building any cache (that is TKT-31); changing any Cache-Control header or TTL value; any code change at all.

uncertainties.note: None. This is a documentation correction against read code; the facts were verified in this review (gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go has no cache; web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts is the only implementation).

dependencies.note: None. Relates to TKT-31 (Epic: Read-path caching & hot-event serving), which owns the actual tier — linked, not blocking.

approach.note: Amend, do not rewrite: the TTL tiers and the single-cache-owner rule are still the right decisions and stay. What changes is the ADR saying plainly that the tiers are today a contract for future caches and bind only the SSR tier. Docs and ADR only — no source changes (this ticket must not grow a code diff).

first_slice.note: The whole ticket is one slice: the ADR-004 amendment plus the architecture.md line. Small enough for risk:low.

success.note: COS: (1) ADR-004 states which readers honor the volatility tiers today — the Astro SSR page-data cache, with single-flight — and that gateway, service-to-service, back-office and scanner reads honor nothing; (2) it says the TTL declarations are a contract for future caches, so no future reader mistakes them for an existing tier; (3) the gap is linked to TKT-31 rather than left implicit; (4) docs/architecture.md's caching line matches; (5) zero source changes in the diff.

context_memo.note: Baked: ADR-004 (the decision being amended — the tiers and the single-owner rule survive, only the claim about coverage changes), ADR-006 (the storefront shell owns the minutes tier — the one place the rule IS implemented, and the model for how the ADR should read). Related epic: TKT-31 read-path caching & hot-event serving.

binding.rule: Public reads declare volatility-tiered TTLs; the read path is cache-first, and each tier has exactly one cache owner so staleness never stacks.

We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only. The gateway is the only public surface, with explicit route registration.

reference.summary: Architecture review R4 — the finding, with the three verified read paths
